The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: convert prose to checks in a single owner-approved PR (a check can break CI or misfire, so it is reviewed, not auto-merged).

## The method lives in the skill

The conversion method — how to spot an always-testable rule in prose, judge convertibility, author the check plus its **see-it-fail** fixture, and decide what stays prose — is owned by the [**prose-to-checks** skill](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This worker only frames the unattended run around it.

## What a run does

1. **Pick convertible prose** under the Context's pack paths — rules that are *always testable* (a deterministic condition a check could assert) and that no existing check already covers. Prefer the strongest, clearest candidates; converting one or two solid rules well beats churning many shakily.
2. **Convert per the skill** — author the rule module in its owning pack, register it in that pack's `pack.mjs`, and add a **fixture test that fires on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one** (see-it-fail is mandatory — a check that can't be made confident is left as prose, never shipped broken). Then apply the skill's **deletion test** to the prose the check now stands beside — a paragraph the check fully covers is deleted whole, never trimmed.

4. **Log to the tracker** — the standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks`** in this repo. Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**; create it already closed if missing. **Never open, close, or reopen it**. Log each run as a **dated comment**: the prose converted and the check id it became, or "nothing convertible this run".

## What this task must never do

- **Never ship a check that can't be made confident** — the see-it-fail fixture is the gate; an unprovable rule stays prose.
- **Never convert a rule an existing check already covers** — dedupe against the check set first.
- **Never touch a pack path outside the Context**, and **never edit a mounted canon pack** under `.claudinite/shared/` — a consumer improves only its own local packs.
- **Run on `opus`** — judging convertibility and authoring checks + fixtures is heavy judgment; this task declares `agent_model: opus`.

---
name: prose-to-checks
description: Mine a repo's existing pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, or when the growth prose-to-checks sweep runs.
---

# Convert existing prose to checks

A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs. The growth *extract* stage converts each **new**
lesson down the promotion ladder; this pass sweeps the **existing** prose backlog for rules that
are always-testable but still live only as prose — and converts them, so the packs keep shedding
context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is first learned. It runs as
grow_with_claudinite's daily `prose-to-checks-sweep` task, and on demand.

## Scope — the pack paths you were given

Work only the **pack paths configured for this repo** (the task passes them in its Context): a
consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by default — projects don't
improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core `packs/`. Read the
prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them). Never edit a
read-only mounted canon pack under `.claudinite/shared/`.

## What to look for — the check-the-world test

For each rule, ask the one question from
[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**

- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.

The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.

## How to convert one

Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:

1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
   doesn't ship.
3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
   directional by kind.
4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
   how you decide which paragraphs those are.

**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
check to the same fixture bar.

When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.

## Coming out: the deletion test

Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.

Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
carries.

The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.

Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
**reader**, not mechanized.

## Bounds

- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
  *landed* check now enforces.
- Run the suite and the sweep green before opening the PR; open it for the owner's approval,
  never a direct push to `main`.

1 # gcec rules 2 3 The project's standing working rules — injected at session start while this pack 4 is declared. Activity-scoped procedures live in this pack's skills 5 (snapshot-approval, merge-and-ci, testing-guide) and surface on 6 demand; the extractor-automation domain's standing rules are the "Extractor 7 pipeline" section below, and its scheduled tasks live under `tasks/`. 8 9 ## Working rules 10 11 - **Never carry uncommitted edits onto a new branch with 12 `git checkout -- `** — that restores the paths' *committed* 13 content, silently destroying exactly the edits it was meant to preserve. 14 `git checkout -b origin/main` already brings a clean working tree along; 15 when it can't, commit or `git stash` first and never in the same `&&` chain 16 that moves the branch. In #734 the combined one-liner wiped three finished 17 edits **and** invalidated the `check_the_world.mjs` + `npm run test:offline` 18 pass that had just gone green, forcing a full re-verification. 19 - **Cap and qualify every GitHub MCP list/search call** — an unbounded one 20 hard-fails the tool-result cap and costs a 2–3-call dig through the saved 21 result file. `search_issues` handed a bare title string full-text-searches the 22 whole repo and returns every match with its full body: the standing 23 `Claudinite tracker: ` lookup that opens every scheduled task blew up at 24 185–211 KB three times (#734 twice, #753), and `actions_list` without a page 25 cap at 155 KB (#760). Qualify the query (`in:title "Claudinite tracker: 26 "`, or `list_issues` + `labels`) **and** pass a small `perPage` (5–10) — 27 the answer wanted is one issue or one run, never a page of them. 28 - **This repo's one divergence from the canon merge recipe: CI must be green 29 first** — twice for e2e/heavy-browser changes. The project mechanics of driving 30 a merge (dispatching CI in a web session, the poll back-off, when to arm 31 auto-merge instead of waiting) are the merge-and-ci skill — **load it for any PR a session opens**, including one 32 opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended run, not only for a deliberate 33 merge. 34 - **`npm run regen` is the regenerator** (load lists + UI snapshots + 35 generic-coverage baseline/report); a stale artifact can't slip through — its 36 own gate fails. On the `ours` driver (kept in sync with `.gitattributes`): 37 `extension/event-extractors/load-order.generated.json` (from `npm run index`), 38 `dev/requirements//cases/*.png` (from `npm run refresh:ui`), and 39 `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json` 40 + `generic-coverage.GENERATED.md` (from the generic-coverage test). The 41 inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — 42 **not** on the `ours` driver; reconcile via `npm run regen` + the gallery 43 drift gate. If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate 44 firing — review it, don't paper over it. 45 - **Keep divergence small**: when syncing a branch to `origin/main` (by rebase — 46 this repo forbids merge commits), **run `npm run regen`** as part of the sync, 47 so the branch carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest 48 sources. 49 - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), 50 link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — 51 `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` 52 — for one-page review. 53 54 ## Owner commands 55 56 - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for 57 the published artifact. The bump mechanics are the canon `bump-version` 58 skill's; honor an explicit target ("bump version to 1.4.0") or level ("bump 59 patch" / "bump major") when given. Open the PR, 60 get CI green, squash-merge with `(#N)` — 61 saying "bump version" is itself the merge authorization for **this** 62 deterministic bump PR only. The merge triggers **Release: Create Package**; 63 do **not** report done until the `vX.Y.Z` GitHub Release with its refreshed 64 `google-calendar-event-creator.zip` asset is published — poll via the GitHub 65 MCP tools on the merge-and-ci skill's back-off (reporting at merge time races 66 the async build). 67 - **"learned lessons"** = run the canon lessons-learned pass over the current 68 conversation on **the strongest model available**, plus the standing 69 efficiency analysis of the conversation's tool/process usage. Only when the 70 owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. 71 72 ## Testing invariants 73 74 - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads 75 `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every 76 required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct 77 behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a 78 supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. 79 - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** 80 (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the 81 path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate 82 departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction 83 tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live 84 cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared 85 infra (not a test) and stays at the root. 86 - **The pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, 87 currently 2026-06-01) **is the floor of the cases' dates**: author a 88 neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or 89 a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. 90 91 ## Codebase gotchas 92 93 Project-wide footguns only. Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon 94 packs/skills. 95 96 - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the 97 lookalike-`hostSuffix` gotcha and the `hostEquals` + dot-`hostSuffix` 98 apex-or-subdomain fix are the canon `chrome-extension` pack's; the real 99 URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only 100 real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). 101 - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here 102 they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why 103 the awaited signal is built from plain promises and the worker publishes 104 `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. Bound every probe and add a 105 test-level timeout regardless. 106 - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 107 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — 108 strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's 109 user-facing text (the generic extractor's footer-address reader does this, #675). 110 - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it** — the parser 111 auto-closes the `

` and the content lands as its `nextElementSibling`; a 112 `.foo p` selector reads `""` with no error. Bit tel-aviv's description blocks 113 (#602) — read the sibling, not the tag. 114 - **The augment-not-replace + reset-per-load rule lands on `GCal` here** 115 (canon): `registry.js` resets `GCal.sources` on load and is pinned **first** 116 in the load order so it runs before any source pushes (#48, #189). 117 - **`clean()` collapses all whitespace including newlines — single-line fields 118 only.** A description run through it loses every line break (#131, #140, 119 #141); multi-line text goes through the block helpers (`blockText` / 120 `normalizeBlock` / `htmlToText`). Line-break handling is generic, never a 121 per-source choice. 122 - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an 123 event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages 124 (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a 125 mere host match. 126 127 ## Workflow-failure classification 128 129 An unattended workflow must converge its failure to a human-visible state (the 130 rule and the `report-failure` reporter live in the canon). **Mind the one gap the 131 check can't see:** `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` only inspects workflows 132 carrying a `schedule:`, so a workflow that is unattended by some *other* trigger 133 — `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch` — needs its failure job wired by hand. 134 The `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is exactly that shape; its 135 reporters live in the vendored create-package/publish/daily workflows it calls. 136 137 ## Extractor pipeline 138 139 Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the two gcec pack 140 [`tasks/`](tasks/): **create-extractor** (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR 141 adding site support, and the sweep that records a committed `.url`'s missing 142 cached page) and the weekly **generic-extractor-improvements** (read a spec only when working 143 on that pipeline). Adding or refreshing a cached live case by hand is the 144 [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) skill. 145 146 - **All page fetching goes through [`scraperapi.mjs`](tasks/create-extractor/scraperapi.mjs), from a 147 task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** A rendered fetch through 148 ScraperAPI's residential proxy (`render=true`, so a single-page app records 149 post-render HTML with real data). Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the 150 portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the 151 `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' 152 `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and 153 never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 154 vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is 155 the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 156 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 157 event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. 158 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 159 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 160 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 161 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 162 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 163 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 164 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 165 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 166 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 167 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 168 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 169 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 170 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 171 from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 172 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 173 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 174 - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't 175 produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's 176 preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason 177 and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch 178 issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it 179 correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. 180 - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** It 181 ratchets up on an unchanged case set and re-anchors when the set changes, 182 compared over the cases the runs **share** — so adding an extractor never fails 183 it (#240) while a pre-existing case that regresses still does. A removed/renamed 184 case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 185 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 186 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 187 be re-anchored over. A source never re-reads what the page 218 already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a 219 specific site. 220 - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** 221 `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts 222 we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second 223 list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as 224 supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host 225 appears in the list. 226 - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to 227 override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — 228 green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 232 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 233 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 234 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 235 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 236 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 237 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 238 239 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 240 241 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 242 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 243 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 244 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 245 246 **Coming out, apply the deletion test: prose a mechanism fully covers is deleted, 247 never trimmed.** Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — 248 *with this paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it 249 describes **and** tell the agent how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete 250 it whole. # gcec rules The project's standing working rules — injected at session start while this pack is declared. Activity-scoped procedures live in this pack's skills (snapshot-approval, merge-and-ci, testing-guide) and surface on demand; the extractor-automation domain's standing rules are the "Extractor pipeline" section below, and its scheduled tasks live under `tasks/`. ## Working rules - **Never carry uncommitted edits onto a new branch with `git checkout -- `** — that restores the paths' *committed* content, silently destroying exactly the edits it was meant to preserve. `git checkout -b origin/main` already brings a clean working tree along; when it can't, commit or `git stash` first and never in the same `&&` chain that moves the branch. In #734 the combined one-liner wiped three finished edits **and** invalidated the `check_the_world.mjs` + `npm run test:offline` pass that had just gone green, forcing a full re-verification. - **Cap and qualify every GitHub MCP list/search call** — an unbounded one hard-fails the tool-result cap and costs a 2–3-call dig through the saved result file. `search_issues` handed a bare title string full-text-searches the whole repo and returns every match with its full body: the standing `Claudinite tracker: ` lookup that opens every scheduled task blew up at 185–211 KB three times (#734 twice, #753), and `actions_list` without a page cap at 155 KB (#760). Qualify the query (`in:title "Claudinite tracker: "`, or `list_issues` + `labels`) **and** pass a small `perPage` (5–10) — the answer wanted is one issue or one run, never a page of them. - **This repo's one divergence from the canon merge recipe: CI must be green first** — twice for e2e/heavy-browser changes. The project mechanics of driving a merge (dispatching CI in a web session, the poll back-off, when to arm auto-merge instead of waiting) are the merge-and-ci skill — **load it for any PR a session opens**, including one opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended run, not only for a deliberate merge. - **`npm run regen` is the regenerator** (load lists + UI snapshots + generic-coverage baseline/report); a stale artifact can't slip through — its own gate fails. On the `ours` driver (kept in sync with `.gitattributes`): `extension/event-extractors/load-order.generated.json` (from `npm run index`), `dev/requirements//cases/*.png` (from `npm run refresh:ui`), and `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json` + `generic-coverage.GENERATED.md` (from the generic-coverage test). The inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — **not** on the `ours` driver; reconcile via `npm run regen` + the gallery drift gate. If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate firing — review it, don't paper over it. - **Keep divergence small**: when syncing a branch to `origin/main` (by rebase — this repo forbids merge commits), **run `npm run regen`** as part of the sync, so the branch carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest sources. - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` — for one-page review. ## Owner commands - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for the published artifact. The bump mechanics are the canon `bump-version` skill's; honor an explicit target ("bump version to 1.4.0") or level ("bump patch" / "bump major") when given. Open the PR, get CI green, squash-merge with `(#N)` — saying "bump version" is itself the merge authorization for **this** deterministic bump PR only. The merge triggers **Release: Create Package**; do **not** report done until the `vX.Y.Z` GitHub Release with its refreshed `google-calendar-event-creator.zip` asset is published — poll via the GitHub MCP tools on the merge-and-ci skill's back-off (reporting at merge time races the async build). - **"learned lessons"** = run the canon lessons-learned pass over the current conversation on **the strongest model available**, plus the standing efficiency analysis of the conversation's tool/process usage. Only when the owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. ## Testing invariants - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared infra (not a test) and stays at the root. - **The pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, currently 2026-06-01) **is the floor of the cases' dates**: author a neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. ## Codebase gotchas Project-wide footguns only. Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon packs/skills. - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the lookalike-`hostSuffix` gotcha and the `hostEquals` + dot-`hostSuffix` apex-or-subdomain fix are the canon `chrome-extension` pack's; the real URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why the awaited signal is built from plain promises and the worker publishes `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. Bound every probe and add a test-level timeout regardless. - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's user-facing text (the generic extractor's footer-address reader does this, #675). - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it** — the parser auto-closes the `

` and the content lands as its `nextElementSibling`; a `.foo p` selector reads `""` with no error. Bit tel-aviv's description blocks (#602) — read the sibling, not the tag. - **The augment-not-replace + reset-per-load rule lands on `GCal` here** (canon): `registry.js` resets `GCal.sources` on load and is pinned **first** in the load order so it runs before any source pushes (#48, #189). - **`clean()` collapses all whitespace including newlines — single-line fields only.** A description run through it loses every line break (#131, #140, #141); multi-line text goes through the block helpers (`blockText` / `normalizeBlock` / `htmlToText`). Line-break handling is generic, never a per-source choice. - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a mere host match. ## Workflow-failure classification An unattended workflow must converge its failure to a human-visible state (the rule and the `report-failure` reporter live in the canon). **Mind the one gap the check can't see:** `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` only inspects workflows carrying a `schedule:`, so a workflow that is unattended by some *other* trigger — `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch` — needs its failure job wired by hand. The `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is exactly that shape; its reporters live in the vendored create-package/publish/daily workflows it calls. ## Extractor pipeline Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the two gcec pack [`tasks/`](tasks/): **create-extractor** (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR adding site support, and the sweep that records a committed `.url`'s missing cached page) and the weekly **generic-extractor-improvements** (read a spec only when working on that pipeline). Adding or refreshing a cached live case by hand is the [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) skill. - **All page fetching goes through [`scraperapi.mjs`](tasks/create-extractor/scraperapi.mjs), from a task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** A rendered fetch through ScraperAPI's residential proxy (`render=true`, so a single-page app records post-render HTML with real data). Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** It ratchets up on an unchanged case set and re-anchors when the set changes, compared over the cases the runs **share** — so adding an extractor never fails it (#240) while a pre-existing case that regresses still does. A removed/renamed case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in `supportedDomains`). ## Architecture rules of the road Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing from a per-site file. - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a specific site. - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host appears in the list. - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. **Coming out, apply the deletion test: prose a mechanism fully covers is deleted, never trimmed.** Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring. Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact carries. The test discriminates rather than just deleting: the `npm test` invariant went entirely (#789 — the check catches it, the testing-guide skill already listed the suites), while the `extension-test/` mirror bullet stays, because `test-offline-list-sync` enforces only the `package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself. Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a reader, not mechanized. **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change without this repo hearing about it. - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a real defect there goes upstream instead. - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose.

1	import testOfflineListSync from './test-offline-list-sync.mjs';
2	import customSourcesFlat from './custom-sources-flat.mjs';
3	import npmTestGlobCoverage from './npm-test-glob-coverage.mjs';
4	
5	// The gcec pack: this project's general working pack, as a LOCAL Claudinite pack
6	// (.claudinite/local/packs/ — tracked project content, discovered and run by the
7	// same engine as the canon packs). It carries the standing project rules
8	// (RULES.md, injected at session start while the pack is declared), the project's
9	// own conformance checks (run at every Stop and in CI alongside the canon
10	// packs'), and the activity-scoped skills that used to live as always-loaded
11	// dev/procedures prose.
12	//
13	// A local pack is always declared by hand in .claudinite-checks.json (never
14	// fingerprinted by --init, never seeded), so detect/marker stay null. Its skills
15	// live INSIDE the pack (skills/<name>/SKILL.md); the engine mounts them from
16	// here, not from the canon skills tree.
17	export default {
18	  id: 'gcec',
19	  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
20	    belongs: "this project's standing rules — owner commands, testing invariants, codebase gotchas, extractor-pipeline rules, architecture rules of the road, capture policy",
21	    excludes: 'general software-engineering practices and portable procedures — those live in the vendored Claudinite canon, not here',
22	  },
23	  detect: null,
24	  marker: null,
25	  prose: 'RULES.md',
26	  worldRules: [testOfflineListSync, customSourcesFlat, npmTestGlobCoverage],
27	  skills: ['snapshot-approval', 'merge-and-ci', 'testing-guide'],
28	};
29

1	// gcec local check: `npm test` runs everything. Its `test` script is a single
2	// `node --test` invocation over a hand-kept list of glob patterns — one per test
3	// directory — so every committed *.test.{js,mjs,cjs} in the repo must be reached
4	// by one of them. The rule this converts is RULES.md's first testing invariant
5	// ("`npm test` runs everything ... `test:e2e` (heavy, CI-only)").
6	//
7	// Why a check and not just prose: the failure is silent in exactly the way a
8	// static scan is for. A test file in a directory no pattern reaches is simply
9	// never run — `node --test` doesn't error on a glob that matches nothing, npm
10	// exits 0, CI stays green, and the coverage is just gone with nothing red to say
11	// so. The pattern list has grown one entry at a time (extension-test/,
12	// dev/build/test/, dev/build/release/, four separate dev/requirements/ subtrees,
13	// the local pack's tasks, the pack's own .mjs fixtures); the next new test
14	// directory is one forgotten glob away from that silence.
15	//
16	// The one carve-out is READ FROM package.json, never hardcoded: the heavy,
17	// CI-only e2e suite is deliberately outside `npm test`, and it declares itself
18	// in `scripts["test:e2e"]`. A file matched by that script's patterns is covered
19	// by design, so the carve-out follows the e2e suite around instead of pinning a
20	// path here.
21	//
22	// ONE DIRECTION ONLY, on purpose (the same choice as
23	// extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js): a *stale* pattern — one
24	// matching nothing — is not asserted, because a literal path that no longer
25	// exists makes `node --test` fail loudly on the next run. Only the silent
26	// direction needs a guard.
27	//
28	// Local-pack check modules are dependency-free on purpose (see
29	// test-offline-list-sync.mjs's header): plain finding objects, no engine imports,
30	// so they also load under the repo's own `npm test` (pack.test.mjs). The engine
31	// already drops the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` canon from ctx.files, so the
32	// canon's own tests are structurally out of scope and need no exemption here.
33	const id = 'npm-test-glob-coverage';
34	const severity = 'blocking';
35	const doc = '.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md';
36	const why =
37	  'node --test never errors on a glob that matches nothing — a test file no pattern ' +
38	  'reaches silently never runs, and npm test still exits 0';
39	
40	const isTestFile = (p) => /\.test\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(p);
41	
42	// The file/glob arguments of a `node --test …` script line. Quotes come off (the
43	// globs are quoted so the shell can't expand them first); the binary and every
44	// flag drop out. A leftover non-pattern token can only ever fail to match, which
45	// under-reports rather than false-alarms.
46	function runnerPatterns(script) {
47	  if (typeof script !== 'string') return [];
48	  if (!/(^|\s)--test(\s|$)/.test(script)) return []; // not a glob-driven runner
49	  return script
50	    .split(/\s+/)
51	    .map((t) => t.replace(/^['"]/, '').replace(/['"]$/, ''))
52	    .filter((t) => t && t !== 'node' && !t.startsWith('-'));
53	}
54	
55	const ESCAPE_RE = /[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g;
56	const STAR_STAR = '\u0000'; // placeholder for a whole `**` path segment
57	
58	// A minimal glob → matcher for those patterns, applied per path segment so `**`
59	// is only special as a segment of its own: `**` spans directories, `*` and `?`
60	// stay inside one segment. A pattern carrying no wildcard and no file extension
61	// is a DIRECTORY argument — `node --test <dir>` recurses — so it covers
62	// everything beneath it.
63	function toMatcher(pattern) {
64	  const p = pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '');
65	  if (!/[*?]/.test(p) && !/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(p)) {
66	    return (f) => f === p || f.startsWith(`${p}/`);
67	  }
68	  const source = p
69	    .split('/')
70	    .map((seg) =>
71	      seg === '**'
72	        ? STAR_STAR
73	        : seg.replace(ESCAPE_RE, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '[^/]*').replace(/\?/g, '[^/]'),
74	    )
75	    .join('/')
76	    // A leading `**/` matches ZERO or more directories — that's what makes
77	    // extension-test/**/*.test.js cover extension-test/host-policy.test.js too.
78	    .split(`${STAR_STAR}/`)
79	    .join('(?:.*/)?')
80	    .split(`/${STAR_STAR}`)
81	    .join('(?:/.*)?')
82	    .split(STAR_STAR)
83	    .join('.*');
84	  const re = new RegExp(`^${source}$`);
85	  return (f) => re.test(f);
86	}
87	
88	const matchers = (patterns) => patterns.map(toMatcher);
89	const anyMatch = (ms, file) => ms.some((m) => m(file));
90	
91	export default {
92	  id,
93	  severity,
94	  description: "package.json's test script globs reach every committed test file",
95	  doc,
96	  why,
97	
98	  run(ctx) {
99	    const raw = ctx.read('package.json');
100	    if (!raw) return [];
101	    let scripts;
102	    try {
103	      scripts = JSON.parse(raw).scripts || {};
104	    } catch {
105	      return []; // malformed package.json breaks npm first — not this check's finding
106	    }
107	
108	    const covered = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts.test));
109	    if (!covered.length) return []; // no glob-driven `test` script — nothing to enforce
110	    const exempt = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts['test:e2e']));
111	
112	    // ctx.files is the whole repo under the engine's default `all` sweep; a
113	    // --changed run narrows it, which only ever under-reports.
114	    return ctx.files
115	      .filter(isTestFile)
116	      .filter((f) => !anyMatch(covered, f) && !anyMatch(exempt, f))
117	      .map((file) => ({
118	        rule: id,
119	        severity,
120	        file,
121	        line: null,
122	        what: `${file} is reached by no pattern in package.json's \`test\` script`,
123	        why,
124	        fix:
125	          'add a glob covering it to the `test` script in package.json — or, if it is a heavy ' +
126	          'CI-only test, to `test:e2e` (which this check reads as the declared carve-out)',
127	        doc,
128	      }));
129	  },
130	};

[{"id":5101138197,"body":"## 2026-07-28

Swept `.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/` (RULES.md + the pack's three SKILL.md files). **Two rules converted**, in PR #776 (`claude/prose-to-checks-sweep-a7f3c2`, dispatch #773):

- **"All page fetching goes through `scraperapi.mjs`, from a task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else" / "Never re-introduce a workflow whose only job is to hold that secret for an agent"** (RULES.md → Extractor pipeline) → **`scraperapi-fetch-surface`** (blocking). Two directions: only the vendored scheduler workflow may name `SCRAPER_API_KEY`; the ScraperAPI endpoint may be built only inside the vendor module (matched by basename, comment lines skipped).
- **"`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file per site, and nothing else"** (RULES.md → Architecture rules of the road) → **`custom-sources-flat`** (blocking). No subdirectory, no non-`.js`, never a pipeline file — `gen-load-order.js` reads that directory one level deep and keeps only `*.js`, so anything else is silently dropped from the load order and never runs.

Both registered in `pack.mjs`, both proved see-it-fail twice — fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fires on a violating input, quiet on a clean one) and a planted violation against the real tree. The now-redundant prose is trimmed to rationale and points at the check; the pack README's rule table moves two rows from *prose* to *hardcoded*.

**Left as prose (judged not confidently checkable):** the `extension-test/` mirror rule (neither direction is clean today — a dozen sources have no mirror test, `extraction.test.js` has no mirrored source), the `REFERENCE_NOW` pinning rule (a wall-clock scan needs arbitrary carve-outs, e.g. the heavy Chrome test's legitimate polling deadline), all of "Codebase gotchas" (runtime knowledge, no static signature), and the process rules (session-start hook, merge flow, branch sync, gallery link — in-flight process leaving no artifact).

Swept `.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/` (RULES.md + the pack's three SKILL.md files). **One rule converted**, in PR #789 (`claude/prose-to-checks-sweep-9k4mzq`, dispatch #786):

- **"`npm test` runs everything"** (RULES.md → Testing invariants) → **`npm-test-glob-coverage`** (blocking). `scripts.test` is one `node --test` over a hand-kept list of ten globs, one per test directory. `node --test` doesn't error on a pattern that matches nothing, so a test file in a directory no glob reaches simply never runs — npm exits 0, CI stays green, coverage silently gone. Same silent-drop shape as `custom-sources-flat`. The single carve-out (the heavy CI-only e2e suite) is **read from `scripts["test:e2e"]`**, not pinned as a path. One direction only: a stale pattern needs no guard, since a literal path that no longer exists makes `node --test` fail loudly.

Registered in `pack.mjs`; proved see-it-fail twice — fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fires on an unreached test file, quiet across all four pattern shapes in use), and a planted `dev/security/csp.test.js` fired end-to-end through `check_the_world` (back to 0 blocking once removed). RULES.md trimmed to rationale pointing at the check; the pack README's rule table gains the row.

**Calibration for this run.** Per the owner's feedback on the reverted `scraperapi-fetch-surface` (a *usage* rule derived from an implementation decision, not a real invariant), the bar applied was: a genuine silent-failure consequence a static scan can catch. Everything below failed it.

**Left as prose — already enforced elsewhere (dedupe):**
- *"every per-site source's host appears in `supportedDomains`"* (Architecture rules of the road) — `extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js` already asserts exactly this, and does it by loading the real sources and running their `matches()` predicates. That beats any regex-parsing check: the 19 sources use at least three predicate shapes (`(^|\.)host$`, `^(www\.)?host$`, an alternation for lu.ma/luma.com, and eventbrite's TLD-open `(^|\.)eventbrite\.`). Nothing to add.
- *"`registry.js` … is pinned first in the load order"* (Codebase gotchas) — `dev/build/test/load-order-generated.test.js` asserts registry-first, helpers-block, orchestrator-last.
- *"Generated files … the committed `.gitattributes` maps each to the `ours` driver"* — the canon's `generated-merge-driver` (basics pack) owns this; widening its basename match is an upstream concern, not a local check.
- *"a new unattended workflow adds a failure job"* (Workflow-failure classification) — the canon's `scheduled-failure-escalation` (github-actions pack).

**Left as prose — judged not confidently checkable (yesterday's rejections re-verified, state unchanged):**
- The `extension-test/` mirror rule — still violated in **both** directions today: `config.js`, `assemble-events.js`, `generic-extractor.js`, `registry.js` and 7 of 8 helpers have no mirror test, and `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js` mirrors no source. Rejection stands.
- `REFERENCE_NOW` (needs arbitrary carve-outs), "Codebase gotchas" (runtime knowledge, no static signature), and the process rules (merge flow, branch sync, gallery link, MCP query capping — in-flight process, no artifact).

**Newly considered this run and passed on:**
- *"The page URL lives only in `<name>.url`, never in the case file"* (testing-guide skill) — scoped and confidently detectable, but the consequence is dead metadata nothing reads, not a silent failure. Below the bar.
- *"a `<kind>/` folder is discovered by its `kind.js`"* (testing-guide skill) — a kind folder with cases but no descriptor would be skipped, but `requirements-coverage.test.js` then fails loudly on the uncovered leaves. Not silent.
- *"`test.yml`'s push trigger covers `claude/**`"* (merge-and-ci skill) — a config fact behind an agent-behavior rule; if it drifted, the prose's own fallback ("only reach for `actions_run_trigger` when no run appeared") self-heals. Below the bar.

---
name: merge-and-ci
description: Drive this repo's PR-to-merged flow cheaply — when to open the PR, how to get CI green in a Claude web session, how to poll without wasting wall time or tokens, and when to arm auto-merge instead of waiting. Use whenever a session opens, watches, or lands a PR here — including one opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended or scheduled run, and any moment you ask "is CI green yet?" — not only for a deliberate merge or an e2e/heavy/UI change.
---

# Merge and CI in this repo

The merge itself: squash, `(#N)` appended to the title, CI green first (twice
for e2e/heavy-browser changes), approval-applies-only-backward — see the gcec
pack's RULES.md. This skill is the *how*: the environment facts and the poll
discipline that keep a merge cheap in wall time and tokens (from a post-mortem
on treating CI as a fixed poll-and-sleep ritual).

## Open the PR early when the only reviewable output is on CI

A change that adds or modifies an e2e/heavy-browser (`dev/requirements/heavy/`)
or UI-snapshot (`dev/requirements/{popup,icon}/`) test can't be exercised
locally — the sandbox has no Chrome — and its reviewable artifacts only exist
on a PR: CI runs the heavy/e2e suites against the branch, and a UI change's
reviewable output (the pixel diff GitHub renders, the inline gallery in the
branch's `dev/requirements/requirements.md`) needs a pushed branch to view at
all. Open the PR early for those.

## Getting a green check in a Claude web session

- **The push-run exists — don't dispatch a duplicate.** A push through the
  in-session git proxy **does** trigger `test.yml`: the workflow's `push`
  trigger covers `main` and `claude/**` precisely so an agent branch gets CI
  without a PR, and a branch that also has an open PR gets a `pull_request` run
  too (two `test` check runs on the same head SHA — the workflow's own comment
  calls that accepted duplication). Merge on whichever is green; only reach for
  `actions_run_trigger` / `run_workflow` when no run appeared at all (a branch
  outside `claude/**`, or a `paths-ignore`/`[skip ci]` push). Firing a manual
  dispatch on top of a run that already exists just buys a third run and its
  wall time.
- **The shell can't observe GitHub state here.** The git remote is a git-only
  proxy (smart-HTTP under `/git/<owner>/<repo>/…`; every other path 400s),
  there's no API token in the env, and `gh` reaches no `api.github.com` — only
  an MCP poll sees check state; a background bash/Monitor loop cannot.
- **Poll on a short back-off, never one long sleep, never tight.** Loop
  **MCP poll → background sleep → MCP poll** until the check leaves
  `in_progress`, backing off **5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, then 30s** repeating — a
  fast run wakes you within seconds, a slow one isn't tight-polled. Always wait
  for the sleep's completion notification before the next poll. While a sleep
  runs, do real work (review the diff, draft the PR body) or end the turn —
  filler calls to look busy are tight-polling in disguise.
- **Don't reach for `subscribe_pr_activity` to wait for green** — its webhooks
  never deliver CI **success** (only failures/comments/reviews), so the
  transition you're waiting for never arrives. It's for babysitting a PR, not
  merge-on-green.
- **Won't sit and poll to green? Arm auto-merge — never end a turn on a
  subscription.** A run that opens a PR it can't watch to the end (an
  unattended/scheduled run, or a fix opened incidentally mid-task) should
  `enable_pr_auto_merge` with `SQUASH` and finish: this repo's
  `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, so GitHub lands it the moment the
  checks pass, with no turn held open and no human in the loop. Ending the turn
  "waiting for CI events" instead strands the PR until a person notices —
  measured, in session `558026a0` (2026-07-24): both `test` runs were green at
  03:58:27Z, the turn had ended at 03:57:56Z on a `subscribe_pr_activity` watch,
  and PR #718 sat unmerged until the owner stepped in **63 minutes** later.
  That one avoidable wait was 85% of the session's 74-minute wall clock.
- **Batch tool loading**: one `ToolSearch` for every GitHub MCP tool the flow
  needs (`issue_write`, `create_pull_request`, `pull_request_read`,
  `merge_pull_request`), not one per turn.

## After the merge, `git fetch origin main` — never check `main` out

The canon merge recipe's post-merge step 5 is
`git checkout main && git pull origin main`. **Skip the checkout here**: a plain
`git fetch origin main` is all this repo's remaining post-merge work needs, and
the checkout is the one part that stalls or gets denied.

Nothing downstream reads the working tree. The capture step that follows the
merge (`capture-log.mjs`) does every branch write through git plumbing against
the *fetched* remote tip and never touches the checkout or the index — its own
header says so. The conformance checks resolve their diff base from
`origin/main`, a remote-tracking ref a fetch alone advances. So the checkout
buys nothing but a working-tree switch nobody asked for, at the very end of a
session that is about to end anyway.

Measured across the four captured sessions, all of which ran the canon step
verbatim: in `295e2230` (2026-07-26) the auto-mode classifier **denied**
`git checkout main` twice — once inside a `fetch && checkout && pull` chain
(08:26:09→08:26:39, 30s) and once alone (08:27:13→08:27:40, 27s) — 57s of dead
wall time plus three recovery calls, after which the session read the capture
script's header and concluded the checkout had never been needed. The bare
`git fetch origin main` in between succeeded on the first try. The same step
cost 44s in `13a6f736` and 8s in `558026a0` for no benefit either. Leave the
tree on the merged branch and fetch.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- engineering-practices: General software-engineering practices — naming by scope, single-source-of-truth with drift guards, GENERATED-file discipline, earning each dependency, verifying real platform behavior. Use before writing or editing code.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- merge-and-ci: Drive this repo's PR-to-merged flow cheaply — when to open the PR, how to get CI green in a Claude web session, how to poll without wasting wall time or tokens, and when to arm auto-merge instead of waiting. Use whenever a session opens, watches, or lands a PR here — including one opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended or scheduled run, and any moment you ask "is CI green yet?" — not only for a deliberate merge or an e2e/heavy/UI change.
- prose-to-checks: Mine a repo's existing pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, or when the growth prose-to-checks sweep runs.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- snapshot-approval: Get owner approval for a moved UI-snapshot baseline. Use whenever a change to a dev/requirements case (its spec or its rendering) makes the snapshot tests fail — the pixels moved and the baseline wants to change.
- testing-guide: Map of this repo's test suites, the requirements model, and where each harness documents itself. Use before writing or changing tests here, adding a requirement case, or debugging a suite — the invariants live in the gcec pack's RULES.md; this is the deeper how-to.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 1	# Prose-to-checks — sweep this repo's pack prose
2	
3	Mine the **existing** prose of this repo's packs — each pack's `RULES.md` / `SKILL.md` — for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Where [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md) descends the ladder for each *new* lesson, this task works the *backlog*: standing prose that was always mechanizable but never converted.
4	
5	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the **pack paths** to sweep. Work only those paths — a consuming repo's own local packs by default; Claudinite also its core `packs/`. **Never** edit a read-only mounted canon pack under `.claudinite/shared/`.
6	
7	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: convert prose to checks in a single owner-approved PR (a check can break CI or misfire, so it is reviewed, not auto-merged).
8	
9	## The method lives in the skill
10	
11	The conversion method — how to spot an always-testable rule in prose, judge convertibility, author the check plus its **see-it-fail** fixture, and decide what stays prose — is owned by the [**prose-to-checks** skill](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This worker only frames the unattended run around it.
12	
13	## What a run does
14	
15	1. **Pick convertible prose** under the Context's pack paths — rules that are *always testable* (a deterministic condition a check could assert) and that no existing check already covers. Prefer the strongest, clearest candidates; converting one or two solid rules well beats churning many shakily.
16	2. **Convert per the skill** — author the rule module in its owning pack, register it in that pack's `pack.mjs`, and add a **fixture test that fires on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one** (see-it-fail is mandatory — a check that can't be made confident is left as prose, never shipped broken). Then apply the skill's **deletion test** to the prose the check now stands beside — a paragraph the check fully covers is deleted whole, never trimmed.
17	3. **Open a PR** — one PR for the run's conversions on a per-run-unique branch, its commit referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes. Keep the repo's offline test suite green before opening.
18	4. **Log to the tracker** — the standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks`** in this repo. Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**; create it already closed if missing. **Never open, close, or reopen it**. Log each run as a **dated comment**: the prose converted and the check id it became, or "nothing convertible this run".
19	
20	## What this task must never do
21	
22	- **Never ship a check that can't be made confident** — the see-it-fail fixture is the gate; an unprovable rule stays prose.
23	- **Never convert a rule an existing check already covers** — dedupe against the check set first.
24	- **Never touch a pack path outside the Context**, and **never edit a mounted canon pack** under `.claudinite/shared/` — a consumer improves only its own local packs.
25	- **Run on `opus`** — judging convertibility and authoring checks + fixtures is heavy judgment; this task declares `agent_model: opus`.
26

1	---
2	name: prose-to-checks
3	description: Mine a repo's existing pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, or when the growth prose-to-checks sweep runs.
4	---
5	
6	# Convert existing prose to checks
7	
8	A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs. The growth *extract* stage converts each **new**
9	lesson down the promotion ladder; this pass sweeps the **existing** prose backlog for rules that
10	are always-testable but still live only as prose — and converts them, so the packs keep shedding
11	context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is first learned. It runs as
12	grow_with_claudinite's daily `prose-to-checks-sweep` task, and on demand.
13	
14	## Scope — the pack paths you were given
15	
16	Work only the **pack paths configured for this repo** (the task passes them in its Context): a
17	consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by default — projects don't
18	improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core `packs/`. Read the
19	prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them). Never edit a
20	read-only mounted canon pack under `.claudinite/shared/`.
21	
22	## What to look for — the check-the-world test
23	
24	For each rule, ask the one question from
25	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
26	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
27	
28	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
29	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
30	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
31	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
32	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
33	
34	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
35	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
36	
37	## How to convert one
38	
39	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
40	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
41	
42	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
43	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
44	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
45	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
46	   doesn't ship.
47	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
48	   directional by kind.
49	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
50	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
51	
52	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
53	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
54	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
55	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
56	check to the same fixture bar.
57	
58	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
59	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
60	
61	## Coming out: the deletion test
62	
63	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
64	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
65	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
66	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
67	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
68	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
69	
70	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
71	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
72	carries.
73	
74	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
75	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
76	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
77	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
78	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
79	went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
80	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
81	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
82	
83	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
84	**reader**, not mechanized.
85	
86	## Bounds
87	
88	- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
89	  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
90	- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
91	  *landed* check now enforces.
92	- Run the suite and the sweep green before opening the PR; open it for the owner's approval,
93	  never a direct push to `main`.
