1 # gcec rules 2 3 The project's standing working rules — injected at session start while this pack 4 is declared. Activity-scoped procedures live in this pack's skills 5 (snapshot-approval, merge-and-ci, testing-guide) and surface on 6 demand; the extractor-automation domain's standing rules are the "Extractor 7 pipeline" section below, and its scheduled tasks live under `tasks/`. 8 9 ## Working rules 10 11 - **Never carry uncommitted edits onto a new branch with 12 `git checkout -- `** — that restores the paths' *committed* 13 content, silently destroying exactly the edits it was meant to preserve. 14 `git checkout -b origin/main` already brings a clean working tree along; 15 when it can't, commit or `git stash` first and never in the same `&&` chain 16 that moves the branch. In #734 the combined one-liner wiped three finished 17 edits **and** invalidated the `check_the_world.mjs` + `npm run test:offline` 18 pass that had just gone green, forcing a full re-verification. 19 - **Cap and qualify every GitHub MCP list/search call** — an unbounded one 20 hard-fails the tool-result cap and costs a 2–3-call dig through the saved 21 result file. `search_issues` handed a bare title string full-text-searches the 22 whole repo and returns every match with its full body: the standing 23 `Claudinite tracker: ` lookup that opens every scheduled task blew up at 24 185–211 KB three times (#734 twice, #753), and `actions_list` without a page 25 cap at 155 KB (#760). Qualify the query (`in:title "Claudinite tracker: 26 "`, or `list_issues` + `labels`) **and** pass a small `perPage` (5–10) — 27 the answer wanted is one issue or one run, never a page of them. 28 - **This repo's one divergence from the canon merge recipe: CI must be green 29 first** — twice for e2e/heavy-browser changes. The project mechanics of driving 30 a merge (dispatching CI in a web session, the poll back-off, when to arm 31 auto-merge instead of waiting) are the merge-and-ci skill — **load it for any PR a session opens**, including one 32 opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended run, not only for a deliberate 33 merge. 34 - **`npm run regen` is the regenerator** (load lists + UI snapshots + 35 generic-coverage baseline/report); a stale artifact can't slip through — its 36 own gate fails. On the `ours` driver (kept in sync with `.gitattributes`): 37 `extension/event-extractors/load-order.generated.json` (from `npm run index`), 38 `dev/requirements//cases/*.png` (from `npm run refresh:ui`), and 39 `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json` 40 + `generic-coverage.GENERATED.md` (from the generic-coverage test). The 41 inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — 42 **not** on the `ours` driver; reconcile via `npm run regen` + the gallery 43 drift gate. If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate 44 firing — review it, don't paper over it. 45 - **Keep divergence small**: when syncing a branch to `origin/main` (by rebase — 46 this repo forbids merge commits), **run `npm run regen`** as part of the sync, 47 so the branch carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest 48 sources. 49 - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), 50 link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — 51 `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` 52 — for one-page review. 53 54 ## Owner commands 55 56 - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for 57 the published artifact. The bump mechanics are the canon `bump-version` 58 skill's; honor an explicit target ("bump version to 1.4.0") or level ("bump 59 patch" / "bump major") when given. Open the PR, 60 get CI green, squash-merge with `(#N)` — 61 saying "bump version" is itself the merge authorization for **this** 62 deterministic bump PR only. The merge triggers **Release: Create Package**; 63 do **not** report done until the `vX.Y.Z` GitHub Release with its refreshed 64 `google-calendar-event-creator.zip` asset is published — poll via the GitHub 65 MCP tools on the merge-and-ci skill's back-off (reporting at merge time races 66 the async build). 67 - **"learned lessons"** = run the canon lessons-learned pass over the current 68 conversation on **the strongest model available**, plus the standing 69 efficiency analysis of the conversation's tool/process usage. Only when the 70 owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. 71 72 ## Testing invariants 73 74 - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads 75 `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every 76 required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct 77 behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a 78 supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. 79 - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** 80 (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the 81 path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate 82 departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction 83 tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live 84 cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared 85 infra (not a test) and stays at the root. 86 - **The pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, 87 currently 2026-06-01) **is the floor of the cases' dates**: author a 88 neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or 89 a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. 90 91 ## Codebase gotchas 92 93 Project-wide footguns only. Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon 94 packs/skills. 95 96 - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the 97 lookalike-`hostSuffix` gotcha and the `hostEquals` + dot-`hostSuffix` 98 apex-or-subdomain fix are the canon `chrome-extension` pack's; the real 99 URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only 100 real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). 101 - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here 102 they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why 103 the awaited signal is built from plain promises and the worker publishes 104 `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. Bound every probe and add a 105 test-level timeout regardless. 106 - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 107 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — 108 strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's 109 user-facing text (the generic extractor's footer-address reader does this, #675). 110 - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it** — the parser 111 auto-closes the `

` and the content lands as its `nextElementSibling`; a 112 `.foo p` selector reads `""` with no error. Bit tel-aviv's description blocks 113 (#602) — read the sibling, not the tag. 114 - **The augment-not-replace + reset-per-load rule lands on `GCal` here** 115 (canon): `registry.js` resets `GCal.sources` on load and is pinned **first** 116 in the load order so it runs before any source pushes (#48, #189). 117 - **`clean()` collapses all whitespace including newlines — single-line fields 118 only.** A description run through it loses every line break (#131, #140, 119 #141); multi-line text goes through the block helpers (`blockText` / 120 `normalizeBlock` / `htmlToText`). Line-break handling is generic, never a 121 per-source choice. 122 - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an 123 event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages 124 (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a 125 mere host match. 126 127 ## Workflow-failure classification 128 129 An unattended workflow must converge its failure to a human-visible state (the 130 rule and the `report-failure` reporter live in the canon). **Mind the one gap the 131 check can't see:** `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` only inspects workflows 132 carrying a `schedule:`, so a workflow that is unattended by some *other* trigger 133 — `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch` — needs its failure job wired by hand. 134 The `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is exactly that shape; its 135 reporters live in the vendored create-package/publish/daily workflows it calls. 136 137 ## Extractor pipeline 138 139 Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the two gcec pack 140 [`tasks/`](tasks/): **create-extractor** (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR 141 adding site support, and the sweep that records a committed `.url`'s missing 142 cached page) and the weekly **generic-extractor-improvements** (read a spec only when working 143 on that pipeline). Adding or refreshing a cached live case by hand is the 144 [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) skill. 145 146 - **All page fetching goes through [`scraperapi.mjs`](tasks/create-extractor/scraperapi.mjs), from a 147 task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** A rendered fetch through 148 ScraperAPI's residential proxy (`render=true`, so a single-page app records 149 post-render HTML with real data). Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the 150 portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the 151 `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' 152 `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and 153 never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 154 vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is 155 the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 156 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 157 event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. 158 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 159 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 160 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 161 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 162 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 163 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 164 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 165 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 166 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 167 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 168 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 169 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 170 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 171 from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 172 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 173 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 174 - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't 175 produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's 176 preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason 177 and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch 178 issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it 179 correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. 180 - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** It 181 ratchets up on an unchanged case set and re-anchors when the set changes, 182 compared over the cases the runs **share** — so adding an extractor never fails 183 it (#240) while a pre-existing case that regresses still does. A removed/renamed 184 case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 185 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 186 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 187 be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers 188 (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). 189 - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — 190 even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call 191 `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see 192 the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` 193 alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every 194 extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's 195 overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its 196 hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction 197 bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, 198 site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating 199 hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the 200 generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a 201 candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in 202 `supportedDomains`). 203 204 ## Architecture rules of the road 205 206 Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update 207 this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is 208 `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): 209 210 - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file 211 per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline 212 itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core 213 generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing 214 from a per-site file. 215 - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs 216 on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over 217 it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page 218 already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a 219 specific site. 220 - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** 221 `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts 222 we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second 223 list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as 224 supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host 225 appears in the list. 226 - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to 227 override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — 228 green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a 229 `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts 230 needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file 231 back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 232 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 233 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 234 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 235 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 236 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 237 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 238 239 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 240 241 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 242 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 243 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 244 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 245 246 **Coming out, apply the deletion test: prose a mechanism fully covers is deleted, 247 never trimmed.** Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — 248 *with this paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it 249 describes **and** tell the agent how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete 250 it whole. The check's failure message is where the rule lives now and its header 251 comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating either pays twice 252 and is the drift trap waiting to spring. Before concluding prose is the only 253 carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an activity-scoped skill often 254 already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact carries. 255 The test discriminates rather than just deleting: the `npm test` invariant went 256 entirely (#789 — the check catches it, the testing-guide skill already listed the 257 suites), while the `extension-test/` mirror bullet stays, because 258 `test-offline-list-sync` enforces only the `package.json` list's sync with the 259 tree and never the mirror convention itself. Whether a check covers a rule is a 260 judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a reader, not mechanized. 261 262 **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a 263 lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: 264 265 - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, 266 summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change 267 without this repo hearing about it. 268 - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't 269 mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a 270 real defect there goes upstream instead. 271 - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry 272 **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is 273 `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. 274 275 None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose. 276

5	
6	# Merge and CI in this repo
7	
8	The merge itself: squash, `(#N)` appended to the title, CI green first (twice
9	for e2e/heavy-browser changes), approval-applies-only-backward — see the gcec
10	pack's RULES.md. This skill is the *how*: the environment facts and the poll
11	discipline that keep a merge cheap in wall time and tokens (from a post-mortem
12	on treating CI as a fixed poll-and-sleep ritual).
13	
14	## Open the PR early when the only reviewable output is on CI
15	
16	A change that adds or modifies an e2e/heavy-browser (`dev/requirements/heavy/`)
17	or UI-snapshot (`dev/requirements/{popup,icon}/`) test can't be exercised
18	locally — the sandbox has no Chrome — and its reviewable artifacts only exist
19	on a PR: CI runs the heavy/e2e suites against the branch, and a UI change's
20	reviewable output (the pixel diff GitHub renders, the inline gallery in the
21	branch's `dev/requirements/requirements.md`) needs a pushed branch to view at
22	all. Open the PR early for those.
23	
24	## Getting a green check in a Claude web session
25	
26	- **The push-run exists — don't dispatch a duplicate.** A push through the
27	  in-session git proxy **does** trigger `test.yml`: the workflow's `push`
28	  trigger covers `main` and `claude/**` precisely so an agent branch gets CI
29	  without a PR, and a branch that also has an open PR gets a `pull_request` run
30	  too (two `test` check runs on the same head SHA — the workflow's own comment
31	  calls that accepted duplication). Merge on whichever is green; only reach for
32	  `actions_run_trigger` / `run_workflow` when no run appeared at all (a branch
33	  outside `claude/**`, or a `paths-ignore`/`[skip ci]` push). Firing a manual
34	  dispatch on top of a run that already exists just buys a third run and its
35	  wall time.
36	- **The shell can't observe GitHub state here.** The git remote is a git-only
37	  proxy (smart-HTTP under `/git/<owner>/<repo>/…`; every other path 400s),
38	  there's no API token in the env, and `gh` reaches no `api.github.com` — only
39	  an MCP poll sees check state; a background bash/Monitor loop cannot.
40	- **Poll on a short back-off, never one long sleep, never tight.** Loop
41	  **MCP poll → background sleep → MCP poll** until the check leaves
42	  `in_progress`, backing off **5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, then 30s** repeating — a
43	  fast run wakes you within seconds, a slow one isn't tight-polled. Always wait
44	  for the sleep's completion notification before the next poll. While a sleep
45	  runs, do real work (review the diff, draft the PR body) or end the turn —
46	  filler calls to look busy are tight-polling in disguise.
47	- **Don't reach for `subscribe_pr_activity` to wait for green** — its webhooks
48	  never deliver CI **success** (only failures/comments/reviews), so the
49	  transition you're waiting for never arrives. It's for babysitting a PR, not
50	  merge-on-green.
51	- **Won't sit and poll to green? Arm auto-merge — never end a turn on a
52	  subscription.** A run that opens a PR it can't watch to the end (an
53	  unattended/scheduled run, or a fix opened incidentally mid-task) should
54	  `enable_pr_auto_merge` with `SQUASH` and finish: this repo's
55	  `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, so GitHub lands it the moment the
56	  checks pass, with no turn held open and no human in the loop. Ending the turn
57	  "waiting for CI events" instead strands the PR until a person notices —
58	  measured, in session `558026a0` (2026-07-24): both `test` runs were green at
59	  03:58:27Z, the turn had ended at 03:57:56Z on a `subscribe_pr_activity` watch,
60	  and PR #718 sat unmerged until the owner stepped in **63 minutes** later.
61	  That one avoidable wait was 85% of the session's 74-minute wall clock.
62	- **Batch tool loading**: one `ToolSearch` for every GitHub MCP tool the flow
63	  needs (`issue_write`, `create_pull_request`, `pull_request_read`,
64	  `merge_pull_request`), not one per turn.
65	
66	## After the merge, `git fetch origin main` — never check `main` out
67	
68	The canon merge recipe's post-merge step 5 is
69	`git checkout main && git pull origin main`. **Skip the checkout here**: a plain
70	`git fetch origin main` is all this repo's remaining post-merge work needs, and
71	the checkout is the one part that stalls or gets denied.
72	
73	Nothing downstream reads the working tree. The capture step that follows the
74	merge (`capture-log.mjs`) does every branch write through git plumbing against
75	the *fetched* remote tip and never touches the checkout or the index — its own
76	header says so. The conformance checks resolve their diff base from
77	`origin/main`, a remote-tracking ref a fetch alone advances. So the checkout
78	buys nothing but a working-tree switch nobody asked for, at the very end of a
79	session that is about to end anyway.
80	
81	Measured across the four captured sessions, all of which ran the canon step
82	verbatim: in `295e2230` (2026-07-26) the auto-mode classifier **denied**
83	`git checkout main` twice — once inside a `fetch && checkout && pull` chain
84	(08:26:09→08:26:39, 30s) and once alone (08:27:13→08:27:40, 27s) — 57s of dead
85	wall time plus three recovery calls, after which the session read the capture
86	script's header and concluded the checkout had never been needed. The bare
87	`git fetch origin main` in between succeeded on the first try. The same step
88	cost 44s in `13a6f736` and 8s in `558026a0` for no benefit either. Leave the
89	tree on the merged branch and fetch.

2	name: testing-guide
3	description: Map of this repo's test suites, the requirements model, and where each harness documents itself. Use before writing or changing tests here, adding a requirement case, or debugging a suite — the invariants live in the gcec pack's RULES.md; this is the deeper how-to.
4	---
5	
6	# Testing in this repo
7	
8	```sh
9	npm install
10	npm run test:live      # integration: the REVIEWED assertions for each supported site
11	npm run test:offline   # unit: internal tests of the extraction logic
12	npm run test:ui        # UI: rendered popup/icon vs. the stored snapshot image
13	npm run refresh:ui     # regenerate snapshots after an intentional UI change
14	npm run test:e2e       # heavy: real Chrome, CI-only (skips without CHROME_PATH)
15	npm test               # everything above except e2e
16	```
17	
18	The invariants (mirror tree, reviewed-contract cases, `REFERENCE_NOW` floor) are
19	always-loaded in the gcec pack's RULES.md. General test discipline (see-it-fail,
20	refusal-test mutation, green-twice, high-watermark gating) is canon.
21	Adding a cached live case is covered under "Live integration tests" below; the
22	generic-coverage gate's invariants are in the gcec pack's RULES.md.
23	
24	## The requirements model — every leaf has exactly one case
25	
26	The spec (`dev/requirements/requirements.md`) is numbered prose; it does NOT
27	tag how a leaf is verified. Each leaf has exactly one
28	`<kind>/cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js` — the **filename** names the leaf, the
29	**folder** names the kind (the single classifier; no `kind` field, no side
30	manifest — issues #429/#435). `dev/requirements/shared/kinds.js` auto-discovers
31	kinds; adding one is a self-contained folder drop (`<kind>/kind.js`). The
32	kinds: **popup** (image, the popup's real `render()`), **icon** (image, the
33	real `toolbar-icon.js` in a fake browser), **behavior** (a click/navigation —
34	no image; verified by `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`),
35	**extractor** (per supported host, real extractor against a real cached page),
36	**logic** (product rules, executable `verify()`), plus `tbd: true` for a leaf
37	not yet faithfully verified. `dev/requirements/requirements-coverage.test.js`
38	fails unless every leaf has exactly one case (and rejects a typo'd/duplicate
39	case, an unknown kind, or a non-image case smuggling in a PNG). Full model +
40	how-to-add-one: `dev/requirements/README.md`.
41	
42	⚠️ The behavior test **stubs** `chrome.tabs.create`/`window.close` — every leaf
43	is *claimed*, not every leaf *faithfully* verified (#435; the banner in
44	`requirements.md` says the same).
45	
46	## Live integration tests
47	
48	`dev/requirements/extractor/live.test.js` is driven by declarative JSON in
49	`expected/`: `expected.events` is the **complete, exact** array the extractor
50	produces — deep-equal on `title`/`start`/`end`/`location`/`ctz`/`details`, no
51	matchers, array length included. The page URL lives **only** in
52	`data/server-fetched/<name>.url` (single source of truth — the recorder and the
53	test both read it; never in the case file). Tests run offline against the
54	committed cached HTML, loaded into a DOM at the `.url`'s URL so hostname
55	detection behaves exactly as in Chrome. `test.yml` never fetches.
56	
57	**Adding one.** Usually you don't: file an `extractor-request` issue with the
58	event URL and the `create-extractor` task records the page, writes the
59	extractor, and opens the PR. To add a case by hand, land the `.url` alone first
60	— a committed `.url` with no sibling `.html` *is* the request the `create-extractor`
61	task sweeps for, so it fetches the page (ScraperAPI; this sandbox is bot-blocked)
62	and opens a PR carrying it. Merge that, then run `npm run test:live` and paste
63	the printed values into `expected/<name>.json` — never hand-write them.
64	
65	**Gardening.** When an event page is taken down, point `<name>.url` at a newer
66	event **and delete the stale `<name>.html`** in the same commit; that is the
67	whole re-record request. Until an HTML file exists, `test:live` fails with
68	`Missing cached HTML for "<name>"`, so land the refresh before (or with) the
69	case's updated `expected`.
70	
71	## UI snapshots
72	
73	`dev/requirements/shared/render/visual-snapshots.test.js` renders each case and
74	pixel-compares (pixelmatch, `MAX_DIFF_RATIO = 0`) against the committed PNG.
75	`render-snapshot.js` picks the renderer by the case's folder: `popup/` → the
76	shipped `render()` path; `icon/` → the real `toolbar-icon.js` under
77	`fake-chrome.js`. Rasterizing is satori + resvg — **not a screenshot**: a
78	constrained flexbox subset that buys determinism with no browser; the renderer
79	folds the real `popup.css` onto the DOM as inline styles (one styling source of
80	truth). Snapshots are authored in **en-US** (a guard test enforces it). After
81	an intentional popup/view/CSS/icon change: `npm run refresh:ui`, commit the
82	PNGs + inline gallery. On mismatch the test writes `.actual.png`/`.diff.png`
83	under `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/` (gitignored) — and a moved baseline
84	goes through the snapshot-approval skill, never silent regeneration.
85	
86	## Where each harness documents itself
87	
88	The *why* of every non-obvious harness decision lives in that file's own
89	header/inline comments (the file-local-footgun rule) — read the file when you
90	touch it; this is just the map:
91	
92	- Generic-coverage gate — `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js`
93	  (field-by-field comparison) + `generic-coverage.test.js` (the high-watermark
94	  gate, #240).
95	- UI snapshot renderer limits (satori/resvg, CSS inlining, tall-list clamp,
96	  `skipRender`) — `dev/requirements/shared/render/popup-renderer.js`; the
97	  pixel-exact diff + en-US guard — `visual-snapshots.test.js`; gestures —
98	  `actions.js`.
99	- Behavior verification (stubbed boundary, self-asserting coverage) —
100	  `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`.
101	- Two-column gallery generator (managed `<!-- req-gallery:<id> -->` lines only;
102	  the file is part-authored, NOT on the `ours` driver) —
103	  `dev/requirements/shared/build-requirements-gallery.js`, gated by
104	  `dev/requirements/shared/requirements-gallery.test.js`.
105	- "Does the extension load?" — two layers:
106	  `extension-test/integration/extension-loads.test.js` (always-on, Chrome-faithful
107	  `importScripts`, #146) and `dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`
108	  (real Chrome, verify via CI).
109	- Requirement numbering is parsed by `dev/requirements/shared/ui-requirements.js`
110	  (numbers only — it does NOT classify leaves).

1	---
2	name: snapshot-approval
3	description: Get owner approval for a moved UI-snapshot baseline. Use whenever a change to a dev/requirements case (its spec or its rendering) makes the snapshot tests fail — the pixels moved and the baseline wants to change.
4	---
5	
6	# Snapshot-approval process
7	
8	The general principle — a moved snapshot/golden baseline needs owner approval,
9	not silent regeneration — is canon. This is the project process when a change
10	to a `dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*` case makes the snapshot tests **fail**:
11	
12	1. **Surface the diff immediately, don't carry on.** Revert the baseline to the
13	   committed **expected** PNG, run the snapshot test so it fails (the harness
14	   writes the rendered `actual` and a highlighted `diff` to
15	   `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/`), and send three images to the chat:
16	   **expected** (committed), **actual** (newly-rendered), and the **diff**.
17	   When the change alters the PNG's **dimensions** (e.g. a fixture shrink),
18	   pixelmatch can't diff unequal sizes so the harness writes only `actual` (no
19	   `diff`) — stitch **expected** and **actual** side-by-side into one image for
20	   the review instead.
21	2. **Ask via `AskUserQuestion`, not prose** — a popup notifies the owner on
22	   mobile. Offer **Approve** and **Reject — let's discuss**.
23	3. **Hold without overwriting the expected image.** If the working tree must be
24	   committed while waiting (e.g. a stop-hook), commit the *reverted* (expected)
25	   baseline so the branch/PR honestly shows the snapshot test **red, pending
26	   approval** — never commit the new baseline first.
27	4. On **Approve**: regenerate the baseline (`npm run refresh:ui`), confirm the
28	   suite is green, and push. On **Reject**: **do not** roll back automatically —
29	   leave the change in place and discuss how to proceed.

1	// gcec local check: `npm test` runs everything. Its `test` script is a single
2	// `node --test` invocation over a hand-kept list of glob patterns — one per test
3	// directory — so every committed *.test.{js,mjs,cjs} in the repo must be reached
4	// by one of them. The rule this converts is RULES.md's first testing invariant
5	// ("`npm test` runs everything ... `test:e2e` (heavy, CI-only)").
6	//
7	// Why a check and not just prose: the failure is silent in exactly the way a
8	// static scan is for. A test file in a directory no pattern reaches is simply
9	// never run — `node --test` doesn't error on a glob that matches nothing, npm
10	// exits 0, CI stays green, and the coverage is just gone with nothing red to say
11	// so. The pattern list has grown one entry at a time (extension-test/,
12	// dev/build/test/, dev/build/release/, four separate dev/requirements/ subtrees,
13	// the local pack's tasks, the pack's own .mjs fixtures); the next new test
14	// directory is one forgotten glob away from that silence.
15	//
16	// The one carve-out is READ FROM package.json, never hardcoded: the heavy,
17	// CI-only e2e suite is deliberately outside `npm test`, and it declares itself
18	// in `scripts["test:e2e"]`. A file matched by that script's patterns is covered
19	// by design, so the carve-out follows the e2e suite around instead of pinning a
20	// path here.
21	//
22	// ONE DIRECTION ONLY, on purpose (the same choice as
23	// extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js): a *stale* pattern — one
24	// matching nothing — is not asserted, because a literal path that no longer
25	// exists makes `node --test` fail loudly on the next run. Only the silent
26	// direction needs a guard.
27	//
28	// Local-pack check modules are dependency-free on purpose (see
29	// test-offline-list-sync.mjs's header): plain finding objects, no engine imports,
30	// so they also load under the repo's own `npm test` (pack.test.mjs). The engine
31	// already drops the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` canon from ctx.files, so the
32	// canon's own tests are structurally out of scope and need no exemption here.
33	const id = 'npm-test-glob-coverage';
34	const severity = 'blocking';
35	const doc = '.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md';
36	const why =
37	  'node --test never errors on a glob that matches nothing — a test file no pattern ' +
38	  'reaches silently never runs, and npm test still exits 0';
39	
40	const isTestFile = (p) => /\.test\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(p);
41	
42	// The file/glob arguments of a `node --test …` script line. Quotes come off (the
43	// globs are quoted so the shell can't expand them first); the binary and every
44	// flag drop out. A leftover non-pattern token can only ever fail to match, which
45	// under-reports rather than false-alarms.
46	function runnerPatterns(script) {
47	  if (typeof script !== 'string') return [];
48	  if (!/(^|\s)--test(\s|$)/.test(script)) return []; // not a glob-driven runner
49	  return script
50	    .split(/\s+/)
51	    .map((t) => t.replace(/^['"]/, '').replace(/['"]$/, ''))
52	    .filter((t) => t && t !== 'node' && !t.startsWith('-'));
53	}
54	
55	const ESCAPE_RE = /[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g;
56	const STAR_STAR = '\u0000'; // placeholder for a whole `**` path segment
57	
58	// A minimal glob → matcher for those patterns, applied per path segment so `**`
59	// is only special as a segment of its own: `**` spans directories, `*` and `?`
60	// stay inside one segment. A pattern carrying no wildcard and no file extension
61	// is a DIRECTORY argument — `node --test <dir>` recurses — so it covers
62	// everything beneath it.
63	function toMatcher(pattern) {
64	  const p = pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '');
65	  if (!/[*?]/.test(p) && !/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(p)) {
66	    return (f) => f === p || f.startsWith(`${p}/`);
67	  }
68	  const source = p
69	    .split('/')
70	    .map((seg) =>
71	      seg === '**'
72	        ? STAR_STAR
73	        : seg.replace(ESCAPE_RE, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '[^/]*').replace(/\?/g, '[^/]'),
74	    )
75	    .join('/')
76	    // A leading `**/` matches ZERO or more directories — that's what makes
77	    // extension-test/**/*.test.js cover extension-test/host-policy.test.js too.
78	    .split(`${STAR_STAR}/`)
79	    .join('(?:.*/)?')
80	    .split(`/${STAR_STAR}`)
81	    .join('(?:/.*)?')
82	    .split(STAR_STAR)
83	    .join('.*');
84	  const re = new RegExp(`^${source}$`);
85	  return (f) => re.test(f);
86	}
87	
88	const matchers = (patterns) => patterns.map(toMatcher);
89	const anyMatch = (ms, file) => ms.some((m) => m(file));
90	
91	export default {
92	  id,
93	  severity,
94	  description: "package.json's test script globs reach every committed test file",
95	  doc,
96	  why,
97	
98	  run(ctx) {
99	    const raw = ctx.read('package.json');
100	    if (!raw) return [];
101	    let scripts;
102	    try {
103	      scripts = JSON.parse(raw).scripts || {};
104	    } catch {
105	      return []; // malformed package.json breaks npm first — not this check's finding
106	    }
107	
108	    const covered = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts.test));
109	    if (!covered.length) return []; // no glob-driven `test` script — nothing to enforce
110	    const exempt = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts['test:e2e']));
111	
112	    // ctx.files is the whole repo under the engine's default `all` sweep; a
113	    // --changed run narrows it, which only ever under-reports.
114	    return ctx.files
115	      .filter(isTestFile)
116	      .filter((f) => !anyMatch(covered, f) && !anyMatch(exempt, f))
117	      .map((file) => ({
118	        rule: id,
119	        severity,
120	        file,
121	        line: null,
122	        what: `${file} is reached by no pattern in package.json's \`test\` script`,
123	        why,
124	        fix:
125	          'add a glob covering it to the `test` script in package.json — or, if it is a heavy ' +
126	          'CI-only test, to `test:e2e` (which this check reads as the declared carve-out)',
127	        doc,
128	      }));
129	  },
130	};

+
+The canon merge recipe's post-merge step 5 is
+`git checkout main && git pull origin main`. **Skip the checkout here**: a plain
+`git fetch origin main` is all this repo's remaining post-merge work needs, and
+the checkout is the one part that stalls or gets denied.

+merge (`capture-log.mjs`) does every branch write through git plumbing against
+the *fetched* remote tip and never touches the checkout or the index — its own
+header says so. The conformance checks resolve their diff base from
+`origin/main`, a remote-tracking ref a fetch alone advances. So the checkout
+buys nothing but a working-tree switch nobody asked for, at the very end of a
+session that is about to end anyway.

+wall time plus three recovery calls, after which the session read the capture
+script's header and concluded the checkout had never been needed. The bare
+`git fetch origin main` in between succeeded on the first try. The same step
+cost 44s in `13a6f736` and 8s in `558026a0` for no benefit either. Leave the
+tree on the merged branch and fetch.

input.title: Prose to checks: the shared pipeline names no supported site
input.body:
Prose-to-checks sweep of `.claudinite/local/packs/` for 2026-07-30 (dispatch #799, standing log #777).

## Converted

**RULES.md → "Architecture rules of the road"**: *"The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction … the generic extractor may never know about a specific site."*

→ new gcec check **`pipeline-site-agnostic`** (blocking): no host declared in `extension/host-lists.json`'s `supportedDomains` may appear in **shipped code** under `extension/event-extractors/` outside `custom/` — the generic extractor, the orchestrator, the registry, and the shared helpers.

It is the other half of `custom-sources-flat`: that one guards *what may live in `custom/`*, this one guards *that per-site knowledge lives nowhere else*.

## Why this is a genuine silent-failure invariant, not a usage rule

A host-gated special case in shared code is invisible to every existing signal: the site it patches works, all 536 offline tests stay green, and no reviewer diff is red. The concrete downstream damage is that the **generic-coverage gate then reports that site as gap-free** — because the gap was hardcoded away, not closed generically — and RULES.md reads a no-gap site as *"a candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in `supportedDomains`"*. So the erosion doesn't just sit there; it feeds a wrong answer into a decision this repo automates. It also ends the property the architecture exists to keep: adding a host is a single-file change.

(Calibrated against the owner's feedback on the reverted `scraperapi-fetch-surface` — that was a usage rule derived from an implementation decision. This is a stated absolute in the architecture section with a real, silent, automated consequence.)

## How detection is kept confident

- **The host list is READ from the repo**, never copied into the check — `supportedDomains` is the one declaration of the hosts we claim, so the check follows it instead of pinning a list that would drift.
- **Comments are blanked**, because citing a site as evidence for a *generic* rule is how this codebase documents itself. All four such citations on `main` today (`stubhub.com` in `generic-extractor.js`, `eventer.co.il` + `visit.tel-aviv.gov.il` in `derive-timezone.js`, `livenation.de` in `embedded-events.js`) are legitimate and stay quiet.
- A small **string-aware scanner**, not a regex: `//` inside a `'https://…'` string is not a comment, so a host hidden in a URL literal is still found. Blanking preserves line numbers.
- Whole-label boundary matching: `notstubhub.combo` is not `stubhub.com`, and the longest list entry wins (`visit.tel-aviv.gov.il`, not the shorter host it contains).
- No dedup conflict: `extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js` asserts the opposite direction (every source's host is declared) and nothing guards this one.

## See-it-fail, twice

- Fixtures in `pack.test.mjs`: fires in the generic extractor and in a helper (line number asserted), fires on a host inside a URL string; quiet on both comment forms, on `custom/`, on a host-shaped substring, on a non-`.js` file, and when the host list is missing or empty.
- Planted a `lu.ma` literal in `helpers/dom.js` and watched it fire end-to-end through `check_the_world` at `dom.js:6`, back to 0 findings once removed. Green against the real tree.

## Deletion test — the prose stays whole

Applied and answered *no*: the architecture bullet carries more than the check does (the base-layer/override contract, and *"a source never re-reads what the page already says about itself"*), and the check only catches the obvious carrier — a host **literal**. A hack keyed on a site-unique selector stays the reader's job, and the check's header says so. So nothing is trimmed; the pack `README.md` rule table gains a row scoped honestly (*"host literals only"*).

## Also in this PR
